task.description:
Design the ISS-201 refactoring: transition() returns TransitionResult{state, emitted_events} instead of just InstanceState.

Key design decisions to document:
1. TransitionResult struct shape: { state: InstanceState, emitted_events: []PendingEvent } — emitted_events are the events the engine decided on (parallel_split, timer_created, etc.)
2. InstanceState no longer carries pending_events — it becomes a pure mirror of what's stored in the DB (tokens, status, variables, join_counters, etc.)
3. Engine remains PURE (zero I/O) — transition() does NOT re-append the trigger event; the orchestrator does that
4. The orchestrator (instance.zig) now: (a) saves TransitionResult.state to DB; (b) atomically persists trigger + TransitionResult.emitted_events in the transaction
5. freeOwnedTransitionState() signature changes — now takes TransitionResult and frees both state+events
6. reconstruction.zig replay callers — iterate events through transition(), collecting emitted_events per step
7. Test implications — every test that calls transition() must destructure TransitionResult; unit tests for the enum variants (timer_created emitted, parallel_split emitted, etc.)

BIG PICTURE: This is the foundational EPIC-2 change. ISS-202 (two-phase merge), ISS-203 (deterministic idempotency), ISS-206 (token multiset), ISS-207 (convergent retry) all build on this new interface. The design must be crystal clear about the contract.
acceptance_criteria: Design identifies EXACTLY which fields move from InstanceState to TransitionResult (and which stay)
Design lists every call site to update (with file+line references)
Design specifies the new freeOwnedTransitionState() signature and what it frees
Design documents the orchestrator persistence contract: trigger + emitted_events in one transaction
Design confirms engine remains pure (no I/O, no re-append of trigger)
Design covers test implications: existing unit tests updated, new tests for emitted-event assertion per event type
Lint passes on the design artefact

result.summary: Type E prose design for ISS-201 TransitionResult. Separates transition() output into TransitionResult{state, emitted_events}. InstanceState no longer carries pending_events. Engine remains pure (zero I/O). Documents all call sites with file+line references, freeOwnedTransitionState() signature change, persistence contract, and test implications.
